A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph-transformer robustness work, with matching core relaxations, node-injection formulation, and retained experiments. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack results on CLUSTER and both UPFD datasets, including accuracy curves and component ablations in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results for further architectures, Reddit Threads, local attacks, homophily analyses, and adversarial training in Sections 6–7 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: v2 adds attack adaptations for GPS's gated message passing and Polynormer's sparse attention, plus an alternative eigenvalue-separation procedure enabling spectral backpropagation (Appendix F.2). It also introduces modified free adversarial training with separate attack/model passes and discrete perturbations (Section 7, Appendix D), substantially extending v1's attack framework.

E1.justification: v2 retains CLUSTER and both UPFD datasets, adds featureless Reddit Threads graph classification under structure attacks, and evaluates local single-victim CLUSTER attacks. These additions broaden the represented graph data and attack tasks beyond v1's global node-classification and graph-level node-injection evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds a single-random-perturbation baseline alongside the retained random-search attack, expands transfer comparisons with GPS and Polynormer and with GPS-GCN on CLUSTER, and evaluates Nettack in the local CLUSTER comparison (Figure 26). Nettack was cited but not evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Reported attack-budget ranges expand from 15% to 50% on CLUSTER and from 50% to 100% on UPFD. New protocols include Reddit's stratified 75/12.5/12.5 split, local attack constraints, homophily measurement, and adversarial-training budgets and replay settings. The original datasets' splits, first-50-test-graph evaluation, and 125 attack steps remain.

E4.justification: The original component ablations and constrained CLUSTER analysis remain. v2 adds comparisons of SAN spectral-gradient alternatives, detailed transferability analyses, tests of whether injected graphs preserve node-centric homophily, and local-attack evaluations with different constraints (Appendix C). These address substantial additional questions about attack effectiveness and meaningfulness.

E5.justification: Both versions report attack averages and standard deviations over four random seeds, including the component-ablation tables. The added experiments and result rows do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice, increased run count, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive architecture, Reddit Threads, transfer, local-attack, homophily, and adversarial-training results. Figure 7 newly reports much greater adversarial-training benefits for Graphormer than GCN. Table 3 adds SAN eigen-backpropagation results, including 54.4 ± 0.6% unconstrained CLUSTER accuracy with attention relaxation. Existing Graphormer/GRIT ablations are retained; rounding of old SAN values is not a result change.

T1.justification: v1 states spectral perturbation approximations and refers readers elsewhere for repeated eigenvalues. v2 adds a discontinuity counterexample and explicit eigenspace-basis construction, derives a minimum-norm eigenvalue-separation optimization (Appendix F), and supplies architecture-specific complexity reasoning (Appendix G.3). Principle II also explicitly requires differentiability almost everywhere.

C1.justification: The claims that GTs can be fragile and require adaptive attacks remain. v2 broadens the attack contribution from three to five architectures and adds a central defense claim: adversarial training can substantially improve GT robustness and enable stronger robust learning than traditional message-passing GNNs (abstract, contribution 3, and conclusion).

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting adversarial-training success to flexible learned attention, Polynormer's Reddit difficulties to missing positional encodings, and homophily results to injection unnoticeability. It discusses adversarial-training overhead and implementation limitations. However, v1's explicit caveat that attacks provide no guarantee of proximity to the optimal adversarial example is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproduction-code link, configuration-file instructions, model-specific hyperparameter Tables 4–12, adversarial-training pseudocode, and numerical settings for spectral gradients and attention. These substantially expand documentation without establishing changes to retained experiments. Conversely, v1's GPU/timing information and explicit CLUSTER block-size disclosure are omitted.

R1.justification: The central positioning as the first adaptive GT robustness study remains. v2 adds focused connections to free adversarial training, prior work on MPNN flexibility, Polynormer, and homophily-based unnoticeability, while removing several earlier positional-encoding and certification references. The existing related-work argument remains largely recognizable.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and methodological exposition are extensively rewritten. Architecture descriptions move from v1's Appendix B into the main preliminaries, and v2 separates evaluation, attack results, adversarial training, related work, and conclusion into distinct sections. The narrative is substantially reorganized beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column to single-column layout. Retained attack plots are redrawn with revised panels, axes, styling, and legends, and duplicated main-text ablations are consolidated in the appendix. New displays include the node-probability illustration, defense and transfer plots, homophily distributions, local-attack plots, and hyperparameter tables.

improvement.justification: The new hyperparameter tables and numerical procedures substantially reduce v1's reproducibility gaps, while broader architecture/task comparisons and local-attack and homophily checks strengthen validation. Section 7 and Figure 7 also add an empirically tested defense. These gains outweigh the loss of hardware/timing details and the explicit optimality caveat, although the broad robust-learning interpretation remains supported chiefly by Graphormer-versus-GCN experiments.
